guardDesignReview.notAGrep: Check 4 extracts the cortexPostPaths array and re-implements the exact matching rule spine.ts applies (upstreamPath === p || upstreamPath.startsWith(p + '/')), then asks whether the seam path would be admitted. A literal grep for 'billing' passes on 'api/brokerage/v1/property-explorer', which reintroduces the permission. Fixture 4b and violation CASE 5 both prove the difference.
guardDesignReview.extractorHardening: The closing bracket is found by depth counting with strings and comments skipped, not by indexOf(']'). Pre-registered falsifier for the two tests that cover this: they must FAIL against the old indexOf extractor or they measure nothing. Measured - nested array: old extractor yields ['api/engagements','api/nested/one','api/nested/two'], admits seam = false; bracket-inside-string: old extractor yields [], admits seam = false. Both non-vacuous.
positiveControlsInEveryCheck: check 1 fails if api/ holds no other pe-* function
check 2 fails if vercel.json does not parse, or has no /api/* rewrites
check 3 fails if there is no 'proxy: {' block, or it has no /api/* keys

guardDesignReview.declaredExclusion: The repo-root api/spine.ts (the command-center copy) is checked when present and its absence is reported as a note rather than silently skipped. It carries no GTM sibling, so its GTM control is downgraded to a note and its seven entries are still tested against the seam path. Verified at source: the root copy's cortexPostPaths has six entries, none of them billing and none of them gtm.
